blocked.facebook: facebook-cli pages commands are gated by PROFESSIONAL_CONSENT_REQUIRED ('Professional consent is required. The rejected Page request did not run.') — the user must accept a Meta Business consent card in chat, which a background agent cannot obtain. Additionally, even with consent, facebook-cli exposes no command to list pages liked/followed by a managed Page (available page commands: list, access, account-insights, drafts, posts only). The personal-profile session itself is connected (facebook-cli me returns the user's profile), but there is no 'liked pages' read path for either the profile or the Page.
blocked.tiktok: Profile page https://www.tiktok.com/@mtcstw loads publicly (200, followingCount=173) but the following list itself is login-walled: /following returns HTTP 302 redirect to login. TikTok's public web API (/api/user/list/?action=follow) returns HTTP 200 with an empty body for unsigned requests — TikTok requires request signing (msToken/_signature generated via JS execution), which is not available here. Third-party mirror (tikwm API) was unreachable from this environment. No fabricated list was created.

note: STAGING ONLY — not wired into the site. Both source lists were inaccessible; nothing was cross-referenced and creators-db.json was not modified.

unblock_options.facebook: User accepts the Meta Business consent card in chat (main agent can then retry pages commands), but note no facebook-cli command exists for a Page's liked/followed pages — a Graph API route or the logged-in browser would still be needed.
unblock_options.tiktok: (a) Open https://www.tiktok.com/@mtcstw/following in the user's logged-in browser (if the user is signed into TikTok there) and read the list; (b) user exports TikTok data via Settings > Account > Download your data, which includes the following list as JSON/CSV, and hands the file to the agent.
